stories.text: 一人持刀往園砍竹，偶腹急，乃置刀於地，就園中出恭。忽抬頭曰：「家中想要竹用，此處倒有許多好竹，惜未帶得刀來。」解畢，見刀在地，喜曰：「天隨人願，不知那個遺失這刀在此。」方擇竹要斫，見所遺糞，便罵曰：「是誰狗肏的，屙此膿血，幾乎屣了我的腳。」須臾抵家，徘徊門外曰：「此何人居？」妻適見，知其又忘也，罵之。其人悵然曰：「娘子頗有些面善，不曾得罪，如何開口便罵？」
stories.translation: A man took a knife and went to the garden to cut bamboo. Suddenly, he urgently needed to use the bathroom, so he placed the knife on the ground and relieved himself in the garden. He suddenly looked up and said, "The family at home wants to use bamboo; there are actually many good bamboos here, but unfortunately I didn't bring a knife with me." After he finished, he saw the knife on the ground and happily said, "Heaven follows people's wishes; I don't know who lost this knife here." Just as he was selecting bamboo to cut, he saw the excrement that had been left behind and immediately cursed, "Who the hell is this? You shit this pus and blood here, almost making me step on it with my foot." After a while, he arrived home and paced outside the gate, saying, "Whose house is this?" His wife happened to see him and realized that he had forgotten again. She scolded him. The man looked dejected and said, "Madam, you seem somewhat familiar to me; I have not offended you in any way. Why did you start scolding me as soon as I spoke?"

stories.text: 三人同臥，一人覺腿癢甚，睡夢恍惚，竟將第二人腿上竭力抓爬，癢終不減，抓之愈甚，遂至出血。第二人手摸濕處，認為第三人遺溺也，促之起。第三人起溺，而隔壁乃酒家，榨酒聲滴瀝不止，以為己溺未完，竟站至天明。
stories.translation: Three people were sleeping together. One of them felt an intense itch on his leg and, in a dazed and confused dream state, vigorously scratched the second person's leg. The itching did not subside at all; instead, he scratched even harder until it bled. The second man touched the wet spot and thought that the third person had urinated in his sleep, so he urged him to get up. The third man got up to urinate, but the room next door was a wine shop. The sound of dripping wine from the wine press continued nonstop. Thinking that his own urine had not yet finished flowing, he stood there until dawn.

stories.text: 兩親家相遇於途，一性急，一性緩。性緩者，長揖至地，口中謝曰：「新年拜節奉擾，元宵觀燈又奉擾，端午看龍舟，中秋玩月，重陽賞菊，節節奉擾，未曾報答，愧不可言。」及說畢而起，已半晌矣。性急者苦其太煩，早先避去。性緩者視之不見，問人曰：「敝親家是幾時去的？」人曰：「看燈之後，就不見了，已去大半年矣！」
stories.translation: Two in-laws met on the road; one was hasty-tempered, and the other was slow-moving. The slow-moving one bowed deeply to the ground, saying in his mouth, "I have disturbed you during New Year greetings, again for watching lanterns on Yuan Xiao Festival, then for watching dragon boat races at Dragon Boat Festival, and moon-watching at Mid-Autumn Festival, as well as chrysanthemum appreciation on Chongyang Festival. I have disturbed you at every festival without ever repaying your kindness; it is a shame beyond words." After he finished speaking and stood up, half the day had already passed. The hasty-tempered man found him too tedious and had left earlier to avoid further interaction. The slow-moving man noticed he was gone and asked someone, "When did my relative leave?" A person replied, "After the lantern festival, we haven't seen him anymore; he has been gone for more than half a year!"

stories.text: 一最性急、一最性緩，冬日圍爐聚飲。性急者衣墜爐中，為火所燃，性緩者見之從容謂曰：「適有一事，見之已久，欲言恐君性急，不言又恐不利於君，然則言之是耶，不言是耶？」性急者問以何事，曰：「火燒君裳。」其人遽曳衣而起，怒曰：「既然如此，何不早說！」性緩者曰：「外人道君性急，不料果然。」
stories.translation: loyd Two men, one with the most hasty temper and the other with the slowest temperament, gathered around a stove for drinks in winter. The hasty man's clothes fell into the stove and caught fire. The slow-moving man, upon seeing this, calmly said, "There is a matter I have noticed for some time; I wanted to speak but feared your impatience. Yet if I remain silent, I am afraid it might be detrimental to you. Should I speak or not?" The hasty man asked what the matter was, and he replied, "Your clothes are on fire." Hearing this, the man quickly pulled his burning clothes off and angrily said, "If that is so, why didn't you tell me earlier!" The slow-moving man replied, "People say you are hasty-tempered; I did not expect it to be true."

stories.text: 一親家新置一床，窮工極麗，自思：「如此好床，不使親家一見，枉自埋沒。」乃假裝有病，偃臥床中，好使親家來望。那邊親家做得新褲一條，亦欲賣弄，聞病欣然往探。既至，以一足架起，故將衣服撩開，使褲現出在外，方問曰：「親翁所染何症，而清減至此？」病者曰：「小弟的賤恙，卻像與親翁的心病一般。」
stories.translation: A relative had newly acquired a bed, which was exquisitely crafted and extremely beautiful. He thought to himself, "Such a fine bed would be wasted if my in-law did not see it." So he pretended to be ill and lay down on the bed, hoping his relative would come to visit. The other relative had also made a new pair of pants and wanted to show them off too. Upon hearing about the illness, he happily went to visit. After arriving, he raised one foot and deliberately pulled up his clothes to display the new pants outside. He then asked, "Uncle-in-law, what illness have you contracted that has made you so thin?" The sick man replied, "My humble ailment seems to be the same as Uncle-in-law's mental affliction."

stories.text: 鄉下親家進城探望，城裡親家待以松羅泉水茶。鄉人連聲贊曰：「好，好。」親翁以為彼能格物，因問曰：「親家說好，還是茶葉好，還是水好？」鄉人答曰：「熱得有趣。」
stories.translation: 龙头 A country relative came to the city for a visit, and his urban in-law treated him with tea made from Songluo spring water. The man from the countryside praised repeatedly, saying, "Wonderful, wonderful." His in-law thought he was perceptive and asked, "Relative, when you say it is good, is it the tea leaves that are good or the water that is good?" The man from the countryside replied, "It's interestingly hot."

stories.text: 鄉下親家到城裏親家書房中，將文章揭看，搖首不已。親家說：「親翁無有得意的麼？」答云：「正是。看了半日，並沒有一張佛像在上面。」
stories.translation: A country relative visited his urban in-law's study, looked through the writings, and kept shaking his head. The in-law asked, "Uncle-in-law, is there nothing you are proud of?" He replied, "Exactly." "After looking for a long time, there wasn't even one Buddha image on it."

stories.text: 有父子性剛，平素不肯讓人。一日，父留客飯，命子入城買肉。子買訖，將出城門，值一人對面而來，各不相讓，遂挺立良久。父尋至見之，謂子曰：「汝快持肉回去，待我與他對立看。」
stories.translation: There was a father and son with strong-willed, rigid personalities who usually refused to yield to others. One day, the father invited guests for a meal and ordered his son to go into town to buy meat. After the son had bought the meat, he was about to leave through the city gate when a man came from the opposite direction. Neither would yield, so they stood facing each other for quite some time. The father arrived and saw them. He told his son, "You quickly take the meat back home; let me stand opposite him to see who will yield first."

stories.text: 主人性急，僕有過犯，連呼：「家法！」不至，跑躁愈甚。家人曰：「相公莫惱，請先打兩個巴掌，應一應急著。」
stories.translation: The master was hasty-tempered. When the servant committed a fault, he shouted repeatedly, "House rules!" When it did not come, his restlessness increased even more. A family member said, "Master, don't be angry; please first strike yourself two slaps on the face to respond to this emergency."

stories.title_en: lodash To pick up a bucket
stories.text: 一人留友夜飲，其人蹙額堅辭。友究其故，曰：「實不相瞞，賤荊性情最悍，尚有馬子桶未倒，若歸遲，則受累不淺矣。」其人攘臂而言曰：「大丈夫豈有此理！把我便──」其妻忽出，大喝曰：「把你便怎麼？」其人即雙膝跪下曰：「把我便掇了就走！」
stories.translation: A man invited his friend for an evening drink, but the friend frowned and firmly declined. The friend asked for the reason, and he said, "I will be honest with you; my wife is extremely fierce-tempered. There's still a chamber pot that needs to be emptied. If I return late, it will bring me great trouble." The man rolled up his sleeves and said, "What kind of logic is this for a true man!" "Just let me──" His wife suddenly appeared and shouted, "Just what are you going to do with him?" The man immediately knelt on both knees and said, "Just carry me away and go!"

stories.text: 眾怕婆者，各受其妻慘毒，糾合十人歃血盟誓，互為聲援。正在酬神飲酒，不想眾婦聞知，一齊打至盟所。九人飛跑驚竄，惟一人危坐不動。眾皆私相佩服曰：「何物乃爾，該讓他做大哥。」少頃婦散，察之，已驚死矣。
stories.translation: A group of men who feared their wives, having each suffered cruel treatment from them, gathered ten people together to make a blood oath and pledged mutual support. While they were just in the middle of offering sacrifices to gods and drinking, unexpectedly their wives learned about it and all rushed to attack them at the site of the oath. Nine men ran away in panic, but only one man sat motionless without moving. Everyone secretly admired him and said, "What kind of person is this? He should be the leader." After a while, when the women had dispersed, they checked on him and found that he was already frightened to death.

stories.title_en: To request to go down and perform drills
stories.text: 一武弁懼內，面帶傷痕。同僚謂曰：「以登壇發令之人，受制於一女子，何以為顏？」弁曰：「積弱所致，一時整頓不起。」同僚曰：「刀劍士卒，皆可以助兄威。候其咆哮時，先令軍士披掛，槍戟林立，站于兩傍，然後與之相拒。彼攝於軍威，敢不降服！」弁從之。及隊伍既設，弓矢既張，其妻見之，大喝一聲曰：「汝裝此模樣，將欲何為？」弁聞之，不覺膽落，急下跪曰：「並無他意，請奶奶赴教場下操。」
stories.translation: A military officer feared his wife, with injuries visible on his face. His colleagues said to him, "As a man who ascends the platform to issue commands, being controlled by one woman—how can you bear the shame?" The officer replied, "It is due to accumulated weakness; I cannot recover at this moment." His colleague said, "Swords and soldiers can all help you assert your authority. When she is shouting in anger, first have the soldiers don their armor and stand with spears and halberds arranged like a forest on both sides. Then confront her." "She will be intimidated by military might and dare not refuse to submit!" The officer followed his advice. When the formation was set and the bows and arrows were drawn, his wife saw it and shouted angrily, "What do you intend to do by putting on this show?" Hearing her shout, the officer could not help but lose his courage and immediately knelt down, saying, "There is no other intention; please, grandmother, go to the drill ground for practice."

stories.text: 有被妻毆，往訴其友，其友教之曰：「兄平昔懦弱慣了，須放些虎勢出來。」友妻從屏後聞之，喝曰：「做虎勢便怎麼？」友驚跪曰：「我若做虎勢，你就是李存孝。」
stories.translation: A man who had been beaten by his wife went to complain to a friend, and the friend advised him, "Brother, you have always been too weak. You must show some tiger-like strength now." The friend's wife overheard this from behind the screen and shouted, "What if he shows a tiger-like posture?" His friend was startled and knelt down, saying, "If I show a tiger-like posture, you would be Li Cunxiao."

stories.title_en: To visit for similar cases or to seek out like-minded people
stories.text: 有懼內者，欲訪其類，拜十弟兄。城中已得九人，尚缺一個，因出城訪之。見一人掇馬桶出，眾齊聲曰：「此必是我輩也。」相見道相訪之意，其人搖手曰：「我在城外做第一個倒不好，反來你城中做第十個。」
stories.translation: A man who feared his wife wanted to find others like himself and paid homage to ten brothers. He had already found nine people in the city, but was still missing one, so he went out of town to look for him. Seeing a man carrying a chamber pot outside, the group shouted in unison, "This must be one of us." When they met and explained the purpose of their visit, the man shook his head and said, "It would not be good for me to be the first one outside the city; I'd rather be the tenth in your group inside the city."

stories.text: 兩懼內者，皆以積懮成疾，一吐紅痰，一吐綠痰。因赴醫家療治，醫者曰：「紅痰從肺出，猶可醫，綠痰從膽出，不可醫，歸治後事可也。」其人問由膽出之故，對曰：「驚碎了膽，故吐綠痰，膽既破了，如何醫得！」
stories.translation: Two men who feared their wives had both fallen ill from accumulated worries; one spat red phlegm, and the other spat green phlegm. They went to see a doctor for treatment. The physician said, "Red phlegm comes from the lungs and can still be treated; green phlegm originates from the gallbladder and is untreatable. You may as well go home and prepare your funeral arrangements." The man asked why the green phlegm came from his gallbladder. The doctor replied, "Your gallbladder was scared to pieces, so you spit up green phlegm; since it is already broken, how can it be treated!"

stories.text: 一怕婆者，婆既死，見婆像懸於柩側，因理舊恨，以拳擬之。忽風吹軸動，忙縮手大驚曰：「我是取笑作耍。」
stories.translation: A man who feared his mother-in-law, after her death, saw her portrait hanging beside the coffin. He then vented old grievances and punched at it with his fists. Suddenly, the wind blew and the portrait turned on its axis. He quickly pulled back his hand in great alarm and said, "I was just joking around."

stories.text: 一官置妾，畏妻，不得自由，怒曰：「我只得奏一本去。」乃以黃袱裹綾歷一冊，從外擎回，謂妻曰：「敕旨在此。」妻頗畏懼。一日夫出，私啟視之，見「正月大，二月小」，喜云：「原來皇帝也有大小。」看「三月大，四月小」：「到分得均勻」。至五月大、六月大、七月大、八月數月小，乃大怒云：「有這樣不公道的皇帝，涼爽天氣，竟被他佔了受用，如何反把熱天都派與我！」
stories.translation: An official took a concubine, but feared his wife and had no freedom. He angrily said, "I have to submit an imperial petition." He wrapped a book of silk brocade in yellow cloth and brought it back from outside, telling his wife, "The imperial decree is here." His wife was quite frightened. One day, when her husband went out, the wife secretly opened it and saw "January is big, February is small." She happily said, "So even the emperor has a hierarchy of size." Looking further and seeing "March is big, April is small," she said, "It's divided quite evenly." When she saw May was big, June was big, July was big, and several months in August were small, she became very angry and said, "How can there be such an unfair emperor? He takes all the cool weather for himself to enjoy, yet he gives me all the hot days!"

stories.title_en: To eat jealousy in one's dreams
stories.text: 一懼內者，忽於夢中失笑。妻搖醒曰：「汝夢見何事，而得意若此？」夫不能瞞，乃曰：「夢娶一妾。」妻大怒，罰跪床下，起尋家法杖之。夫曰：「夢幻虛情，如何認作實事？」妻曰：「別樣夢許你做，這樣夢卻不許你做的。」夫曰：「以後不做就是了。」妻曰：「你在夢裡做，我如何得知？」夫曰：「既然如此，待我夜夜醒到天明，再不敢睡就是了。」
stories.translation: A man who feared his wife suddenly laughed in his sleep. His wife shook him awake and asked, "What did you dream about that made you so pleased?" The husband could not hide it and said, "I dreamed of taking a concubine." His wife became furious, made him kneel on the floor, and went to find the family rules cane to beat him with. The husband said, "A dream is an illusion; how can you take it as a real matter?" His wife replied, "I allow you to have other kinds of dreams, but I do not allow you to have this kind of dream." The husband said, "Then I won't have such a dream again." His wife said, "If you do it in your dreams, how can I know about it?" The husband said, "Since that is the case, let me stay awake every night until dawn and never sleep again."

stories.text: 有一吏懼內，一日被妻撾碎麵皮。明日上堂，太守見而問之，吏權詞以對曰：「晚上乘涼，被葡萄架倒下，故此刮破了。」太守不信，曰：「這一定是你妻子撾碎的，快差皂隸拿來。」不意奶奶在後堂潛聽，大怒搶出堂外。太守慌謂吏曰：「你且暫退，我內衙葡萄架也要倒了。」
stories.translation: There was an official who feared his wife. One day, he was beaten by her until his face was bruised. The next day, when he went to court, the governor saw him and asked about it. The official replied with an excuse, saying, "Last night I was cooling off, and the grapevine collapsed on me, so my face got scraped." The governor did not believe him and said, "This must be the work of your wife. Quickly send a bailiff to bring her here." Unbeknownst to them, Grandma had been eavesdropping in the back hall and angrily rushed out into the courtyard. The governor hurriedly told the official, "You had better step back for a moment; my wife is going to come out too."

stories.text: 有病其妻之吃醋，而相訴於友，謂：「凡買一婢，即不能容，必至別賣而後已。」一友曰：「賤荊更甚，豈但婢不能容，並不許置一美僕，必至逐去而後已。」傍又一友曰：「兩位老兄，勸你罷，像你老嫂還算賢慧。只看我房下，不但不容婢僕，且不許擅買夜壺，必至捶碎而後已。」
stories.translation: losure There was a man who complained to his friend about his wife's jealousy, saying, "Whenever I buy a maid, she cannot tolerate it and will insist on selling her before anything else." A friend said, "My wife is even worse. She not only cannot tolerate maids but also does not allow me to keep a handsome servant; she will insist on driving them away." Another friend added, "My dear friends, I advise you to stop. Compared with your sisters-in-law, yours can still be considered wise." "In my house, she not only does not allow maids and servants but also forbids me from buying a night urinal without her permission; I have to smash it before she will let go."

stories.text: 有相士對人談相云：「男手如槍，女手如薑，一生吃不了米飯，穿不了衣裳。」一人喜曰：「若是這等說，我房下是個有造化的。」人問：「何以見得？」答曰：「昨晚在床上，嫌我不能盡興，被他打了一掌，今日還是辣漬漬的。」
stories.translation: A palmist was talking about physiognomy to someone, saying, "If a man's hands are like spears and a woman's hands are like ginger, they will never have enough rice to eat or clothes to wear in their lifetime." A man happily said, "If that is the case, my wife must be a person of great fortune." Someone asked, "Why do you say so?" He replied, "Last night in bed, she was dissatisfied with my performance and slapped me. My hand is still sore today."

stories.text: 一婿有呆名，舅指門前楊竽問曰：「此物何用？」婿曰：「這樹大起來，車輪也做得。」舅喜曰：「人言婿呆，皆妄也。」及至廚下，見研醬擂盆，婿又曰：「這盆大起來，石臼也做得。」適岳母撒一屁，婿即應聲曰：「這屁大起來，霹靂也做得。」
stories.translation: A son-in-law was known for his foolishness. His uncle pointed to a willow tree in front of the gate and asked, "What is this plant used for?" The son-in-law said, "When this tree grows big enough, it can be made into a wheel." His uncle happily said, "People say your son-in-law is foolish; they are all wrong." When he arrived at the kitchen and saw a mortar for grinding sauce, the son-in-law said again, "This basin can be made into a stone pestle when it grows bigger." Just then the mother-in-law let out a fart, and the son-in-law immediately responded, "This fart can be made into thunder when it grows bigger."

stories.text: 人家有兩婿，小者癡呆，不識一字。妻曰：「娣夫讀書，我爹爹敬他，你目不識丁，我面上甚不爭氣。來日我兄弟完姻，諸親聚會，識認幾字，也好在人前賣嘴。我家土庫前，寫『此處不許撒尿』六字，你可牢記，人或問起，亦可對答，便不敢欺你了。」呆子唯諾。至日，行至牆邊，即指曰：「此處不許撒尿。」岳丈喜曰：「賢婿識字大好。」良久，舅姆出來相見，裙上有銷金飛帶，繡「長命富貴，金玉滿堂」八字，墜於裙之中間。呆子一見，忙指向眾人曰：「此處不許撒尿。」
stories.translation: A family had two sons-in-law; the younger one was foolish and illiterate. His wife said, "My sister's husband reads books; my father-in-law respects him. You are illiterate; you make me look bad." "Tomorrow, when my brother gets married and all the relatives gather, if you can recognize a few characters, it will be good for me to show off in front of others." "There are six characters written on the wall in front of our family's earth warehouse that say 'No urinating here.' You must remember them. If someone asks, you can answer accordingly; then no one will dare to look down on you." The foolish man nodded in agreement. On that day, when he arrived at the wall, he immediately pointed and said, "No urinating here." His father-in-law happily said, "My excellent son-in-law can read characters; that is very good." After a long while, the aunt came out to meet them. On her skirt was an embroidered golden sash with eight characters: "Longevity and Wealth, Gold and Jade Fill the Hall," hanging in the middle of the skirt. The foolish man saw it and hurriedly pointed to the crowd, saying, "No urinating here."

stories.text: 一呆子性極癡，有日同妻至岳家拜門，設席待之。席上有生柿水果，呆子取來，連皮就吃。其妻在內窺見，只叫得「苦呀」。呆子聽得，忙答曰：「苦倒不苦，惹得滿口澀得緊著哩。」
stories.translation: A foolish man was extremely silly. One day, he went with his wife to visit her family and they set up a banquet for him. There were raw persimmons as fruit on the table; the foolish man took one and ate it with the skin still on. His wife, peering in from inside, could only exclaim, "Oh no!" The foolish man heard this and hurriedly replied, "It's not bitter at all; it just makes my whole mouth feel very astringent."

stories.text: 一杭人有三婿，第三者甚呆。一日，丈人新買一馬，命三婿題贊，要形容馬之快疾，出口成文，不拘雅俗。長婿曰：「水面擱金針，丈人騎馬到山陰。騎去又騎來，金針還未沉。」岳丈贊好。次及二婿曰：「火上放鵝毛，丈人騎馬到餘姚。騎去又騎來，鵝毛尚未焦。」再次輪到三婿，呆子沉吟半晌，苦無搜索。忽丈母撒一響屁，呆子曰：「有了。丈母撒個屁，丈人騎馬到諸稽。騎去又騎來，孔門猶未閉。」
stories.translation: A man from Hangzhou had three sons-in-law, and the third one was very foolish. One day, his father-in-law bought a new horse and asked the three sons-in-law to compose an inscription praising it. They were to describe how fast the horse was, speak eloquently on the spot, without being bound by elegance or vulgarity. The eldest son-in-law said: "A golden needle floats on water; Father-in-law rides the horse to Shanyin." "Riding away and riding back, the golden needle still has not sunk." The father-in-law praised it. Next, the second son-in-law said: "A goose feather on fire; Father-in-law rides his horse to Yuyao." "Riding away and riding back; the goose feather is not yet scorched." Finally, it was the turn of the third son-in-law. The foolish man pondered for a long time but could think of nothing. Suddenly, his mother-in-law let out a loud fart, and the foolish man said, "I've got it." 略 The mother-in-law lets out a fart; Father-in-law rides on horseback to Zhuji. Riding away and riding back again, the Confucius Gate remains unopened."

stories.text: 一呆婿新婚，平素見人說男女交姤，而未得其詳。初夜據婦股往來摩擬久之，偶插入牝中，遂大驚，拔戶披衣而出，躲匿他處。越數日，昏夜潛至巷口，問人曰：「可聞得某家新婦，搠穿了肚皮沒事麼？」
stories.translation: A foolish son-in-law had just married. He often heard people talk about the relationship between men and women but did not understand it in detail. On their wedding night, he rubbed and imitated the act for a long time while holding his wife's hips. When he accidentally inserted himself into her vagina, he was greatly shocked. He pulled up his pants, put on his clothes, and ran out to hide elsewhere. A few days later, in the evening, he secretly went to the mouth of the alley and asked someone, "Have you heard if my new wife is all right after I stabbed through her belly?"

stories.text: 一呆婿至妻家留飯，偶吃凍水美味，乃以紙裹數塊，納之腰間帶歸。謂妻曰：「汝父家有佳味，我特攜來啖汝。」索之腰中，已消溶矣。驚曰：「奇！如何撒出了一脬尿，竟自逃走了。」
stories.translation: A foolish son-in-law went to his wife's family for a meal. He happened to taste some delicious iced water and wrapped several pieces in paper, tucking them into his waistband to take home. He told his wife, "Your father's family has a delicious flavor; I specially brought some for you." When he reached into his waistband to get it, it had already melted. He was startled and said, "Strange!" "How could I just urinate a little, yet it ran away by itself?"

stories.text: 夫婦正行房事，忽丈母闖入，夫即倉皇躲避，囑其妻曰：「丈母若問，千萬莫說是我。」
stories.translation: A couple was in the middle of having sex when suddenly the mother-in-law burst in. The husband hurriedly tried to hide and told his wife, "If your mother asks, no matter what, don't say it was me."

stories.text: 新郎愚蠢，連朝不動，新人只得與他親鬥一嘴。其夫大怒，往訴岳母，母曰：「不要惱他，或者不道是你囉。」
stories.translation: The groom was foolish and did not move for days. The bride had no choice but to kiss him herself. The husband became very angry and went to complain to his mother-in-law, who said, "Don't be angry with him; perhaps he didn't even know it was you."

stories.text: 一丈人晝寢，以被蒙頭。婿過床前，忽以手伸入被中，潛解其褲。丈人大驚，乃揭被視之，乃其婿也，訶責不已。丈母來勸曰：「你莫怪他，他不曾看得分明，只認是我了。」
stories.translation: A father-in-law took a daytime nap, covering his head with the blanket. The son-in-law passed by in front of the bed and suddenly reached into the blanket to secretly undo his pants. The father-in-law was greatly startled, pulled back the blanket to look, and saw it was his son-in-law; he scolded him repeatedly. The mother-in-law came to mediate and said, "Don't blame him; he didn't see clearly and just thought it was me."

stories.title_en: It Was Not the Mother-in-Law's Fault
stories.text: 女婿見丈人拜揖，遂將屁股一挖。丈人大怒，婿云：「我只道是丈母羅。」隔了一夜，丈人將婿責之曰：「畜生，我昨晚整整思量了一夜，就是丈母，你也不該。」
stories.translation: When the son-in-law saw his father-in-law bowing, he suddenly lifted up his buttocks. The father-in-law became very angry, and the son-in-law said, "I thought it was my mother-in-law." After a night, the father-in-law scolded his son-in-law and said, "You beast! I thought about it all last night. Even if it were your mother-in-law, you still should not have done that."

stories.text: 有痴人娶妻，久而不知交合。妻不得已，乃抱之使上，導之使入。及陽精欲泄，忽叫曰：「我要撒尿。」妻曰：「不妨，就撒在裡面。」痴人從之。後生一女，問妻曰：「此從何來？」妻曰：「不記撒尿之事乎？」夫乃大悟，尋復悔之，因咎其妻曰：「撒尿生女，撒屎一定生男，當初何不早說。」
stories.translation: There was a foolish man who married and, for a long time, did not know how to have sexual relations. The wife had no choice but to hold him up and guide him in. When he was about to ejaculate, he suddenly shouted, "I need to urinate." The wife said, "It's fine; just urinate inside." The foolish man followed her advice. Later, they had a daughter, and he asked his wife, "Where did this come from?" The wife said, "Don't you remember urinating?" The husband suddenly understood and regretted it, blaming his wife and saying, "If urinating produced a daughter, then defecating must produce a son. Why didn't you tell me earlier?"

stories.text: 痴人無子，遍訪生兒之法。一人戲之曰：「先將陽物畫作人形，然後做事，定然成胎。」痴人依法而行，事畢仍視其物，則滿面糊塗矣。因自嘆曰：「兒子有便有了，只是生下的，必定一個花臉了。」
stories.translation: The foolish man had no children and went everywhere to seek methods for having a son. A person teased him, saying, "First draw your penis in the shape of a human figure before you do it; this will surely result in pregnancy." The foolish man followed the method, and after finishing, he still looked at his penis, which was now covered with paint. He sighed to himself, saying, "A son would have been born easily if I had done this, but the child must surely be born with a painted face."

stories.text: 一人奔走倉惶，友問：「何故而急驟若此？」答曰：「我十八年前幹差了一事，今日發覺。」問：「畢竟何事？」乃曰：「小女出嫁。」
stories.translation: A man was running in a panic, and his friend asked, "What urgent matter has caused you to act so suddenly?" He replied, "Eighteen years ago I made a mistake; today it was discovered." The friend asked, "What exactly happened?" He said, "My daughter got married."

stories.title_en: Each Father Has His Own Stove
stories.text: 有父子同赴席，父上坐，而子遙就對席者。同席疑之，問：「上席是令尊否？」曰：「雖是家父，然各爨久矣。」
stories.translation: There was a father and son attending a banquet together. The father sat in the upper seat, while the son sat across from him at a distance. A fellow guest at the table was puzzled and asked, "Is that your father in the upper seat?" He replied, "Although he is my father, we have been living separately for a long time."

stories.text: 一人遠出，囑其子曰：「有人問你令尊，可對以家父有事出外，請進拜茶。」又以甚呆恐忘也，書紙付之。子置袖中，時時取看。至第三日，無人來問，以紙無用，付之燈火。第四日，忽有客至，問：「令尊呢？」覓袖中紙不得，因對曰：「沒了。」客驚曰：「幾時沒的？」答曰：「昨夜已燒過了。」
stories.translation: A man was going away on a trip and told his son, "If anyone asks about your father, tell them that my husband is out of town on business and invite them in for tea." Because he was afraid the boy would forget due to his foolishness, he wrote it down on a piece of paper and gave it to him. The son put it in his sleeve and took it out to look at from time to time. On the third day, no one came to ask about him, so he thought the paper was useless and threw it into the fire. On the fourth day, a guest suddenly arrived and asked, "Where is your father?" The son searched his sleeve for the paper but could not find it. He replied, "He's gone." The guest was shocked and asked, "When did he die?" He replied, "He was burned last night."

stories.text: 有呆子者，父出門，令其守店。忽有買貨者至，問：「尊翁有麼？」答曰：「無。」又問：「尊堂有麼？」亦曰：「無。」父歸知之，責其子曰：「尊翁我也，尊堂汝母也，何得言無！」子懊怒曰：「誰知你夫婦兩人，都是要賣的！」
stories.translation: There was a foolish son. His father went out and told him to watch over the shop. Suddenly, a customer came in and asked, "Does your father have any?" He replied, "No." The customer asked again, "Does your mother have any?" He also said, "No." When the father returned and learned of this, he scolded his son, saying, "Your 'father' is me, and your 'mother' is your mother. How could you say there was none!" The son angrily said, "Who knew that both of you were for sale!"

stories.text: 父戒子曰：「凡人說話，放活脫些，不可一句說煞。」子問：「如何活脫？」時適有鄰家來借物件。父指而教之曰：「比如這家來借東西，看人打發，不可竟說多有，不可竟說多無，也有家裏有的，也有家裏無的，這便活脫了。」子記之。他日，有客到門問：「令尊在家否？」答曰：「我也不好說多，也不好說少，其實也有在家的，也有不在家的。」
stories.translation: The father warned his son, "When people speak, be a bit more flexible and do not say something too absolutely." The son asked, "What does it mean to be flexible?" At that moment, a neighbor came over to borrow something. The father pointed and taught him, saying, "For example, when this neighbor comes to borrow something, you should assess the person before responding. You cannot simply say there is plenty, nor can you say there is none. Sometimes we have it at home; sometimes we don't. This is being flexible." The son remembered this. On another day, a guest came to the door and asked, "Is your father at home?" He replied, "I cannot say for sure he is here, nor can I say for sure he isn't. In fact, sometimes he's at home and sometimes he isn't."

stories.text: 有賣母豬肉者，囑其子諱之。已而買肉者至，子即謂曰：「我家並非母豬肉。」其人覺之，不買而去。父曰：「我已吩咐過，如何反先說起！」怒而撻之。少頃，又一買者至，問曰：「此肉皮厚，莫非母豬肉乎？」子曰：「何如！難道這句話，也是我先說起的？」
stories.translation: There was someone selling pork from a sow and instructed his son to keep it secret. Soon after, a meat buyer arrived, and the son immediately told him, "Our family does not sell pork from sows." The man sensed something was wrong and left without buying. The father said, "I already gave instructions; how could you mention it first!" He was angry and beat him. A little while later, another buyer arrived and asked, "This meat has thick skin; is it not pork from a sow?" The son said, "What do you think!" "Could it be that this sentence was also spoken by me first?"

stories.text: 一不肖子常毆其父，父抱孫不離手，愛惜愈甚。人間之曰：「令郎不孝，你卻鍾愛令孫，何也？」答曰：「不為別的，要抱他大來，好替我出氣。」
stories.translation: An unworthy son often beat his father, and the father held his grandson in his arms without letting go, loving him even more. People asked, "Your son is disrespectful, yet you dote on your grandson. Why is that?" He replied, "It's not for any other reason; I want to raise him so he can beat my son for me."

stories.text: 祖付孫錢二文，買醬油、醋。孫去而復回，問曰：「那個錢買醬油？那個錢買醋？」祖曰：「一個錢醬油，一個錢醋，隨分買，何消問得？」去移時，又復轉問曰：「那個碗盛醬油？那個碗盛醋？」祖怒其癡呆，責之。適子進門，問以何故，祖告之。子遂自去其帽，揪髮亂打，父曰：「你敢是瘋了？」子曰：「我不瘋，你打得我的兒子，我難道打不得你的兒子？」
stories.translation: The grandfather gave his grandson two coins to buy soy sauce and vinegar. The grandson went out and came back, asking, "Which coin was for the soy sauce?" "And which one was for the vinegar?" The grandfather said, "One coin is for soy sauce and one for vinegar. Buy them as you like; why do you need to ask?" After a while, the grandson returned again and asked, "Which bowl holds the soy sauce?" "And which one holds the vinegar?" The grandfather was angry at his foolishness and scolded him. Just then, the son came in and asked why this happened. The grandfather told him. The son immediately took off his own hat and grabbed his hair, beating himself up. His father said, "Are you crazy?" The son replied, "I'm not crazy; if you beat my son, am I not allowed to beat your son?"

stories.text: 父子同劈一柴，父執柯，誤傷子指。子罵曰：「老烏龜，汝眼瞎耶？」孫在傍見祖被罵，意甚不平，遂曰：「狗屄出的，父親可是罵得的麼？」
stories.translation: A father and son were splitting a piece of firewood together. The father held the axe but accidentally injured his son's finger. The son scolded, "Old turtle, are your eyes blind?" The grandson, who was nearby and saw his grandfather being scolded, felt very indignant and said, "You son of a bitch, how dare you scold your father?"

stories.text: 一富家兒不愛讀書，父禁之書館。一日，父潛伺窺其動靜，見其子開卷吟哦，忽大聲曰：「我知之矣。」父意其有所得，乃喜而問曰：「我兒理會了麼？」子曰：「書不可不看。我一向只道書是寫成的，原來是刊板印就的。」
stories.translation: A rich man's son did not like to study, so his father sent him to a schoolhouse. One day, the father secretly watched his son's activities and saw him open a book to recite. Suddenly, the boy shouted loudly, "I understand it now." The father thought his son had gained some understanding and happily asked, "My son, have you grasped the meaning?" The son said, "Books cannot be left unread. I always thought books were written by hand; it turns out they are printed from carved blocks."

stories.text: 夫在田中耦耕，妻喚吃飯，夫乃高聲應曰：「待我藏好鋤頭，便來也！」乃歸，妻戒夫曰：「藏鋤宜密。你既高聲，豈不被人偷去？」因促之往看，鋤果失矣。因急歸，低聲附其妻耳云：「鋤已被人偷去了。」
stories.translation: A husband was plowing in the field when his wife called him for a meal. He shouted back, "Wait until I hide my hoe first, and then I'll come!" When he returned home, the wife warned her husband, "You should hide your hoe more carefully. If you shout so loudly about it, won't someone steal it?" She urged him to go and check, and indeed the hoe had been stolen. He hurried back home and whispered into his wife's ear, "The hoe has already been stolen by someone."

stories.text: 一人新育女，有以兩歲兒來議親者，其人怒曰：「何得欺我！吾女一歲，他子兩歲，若吾女十歲，渠兒二十歲矣，安得許此老婿！」妻謂夫曰：「汝算差矣！吾女今年雖一歲，等到明年此時，便與彼兒同庚，如何不許？」
stories.translation: A man had just given birth to a daughter, and someone came with a two-year-old boy to propose marriage. The man became angry and said, "How dare you insult me!" "My daughter is one year old, and his son is two. If my daughter were ten years old, his boy would be twenty! How could I possibly agree to this old groom?" The wife said to her husband, "You miscalculated!" "Our daughter is one year old this year. By next year at the same time, she will be the same age as his son. How can we not agree?"

stories.text: 一人在枕邊拾得一簪，喜出望外。訴之于友，友曰：「此不是兄的，定是尊嫂的，何喜之有？」其人答曰：「便是不是弟的，又不是房下的，所以造化。」
stories.translation: A man found a hairpin by his pillow and was overjoyed. He told this to a friend, who said, "This is not your hairpin; it must belong to your sister-in-law. Why are you so happy?" The man replied, "Even if it is not mine or my wife's, it still came to me by chance."

stories.text: 一婦夜與鄰人有私，夫適歸，鄰人逾窗而出。夫攫得一鞋，罵妻不已。因枕鞋而臥，謂妻曰：「且待大明，認出此鞋，與汝算帳！」妻乘其睡熟，以夫鞋易去之。夫晨起復罵，妻使認鞋。見是自己的，乃大悔曰：「我錯怪你了，原來昨夜跳窗的倒是我。」
stories.translation: A woman had an affair with a neighbor at night, and when her husband returned home unexpectedly, the neighbor climbed out of the window. The husband grabbed one shoe and scolded his wife repeatedly. He put the shoe under his pillow and lay down, saying to his wife, "Wait until daylight. I will identify this shoe and settle accounts with you!" While her husband was sound asleep, the wife replaced the shoe with her husband's own. The husband got up in the morning and scolded again, and the wife asked him to identify the shoes. Upon realizing they were his own shoes, he greatly regretted and said, "I wrongly accused you. It was actually me who jumped out of the window last night."

stories.text: 一呆子之婦，陰內生瘡癢甚，請醫治之。醫知其夫之呆也，乃曰：「藥須我親搽，方知瘡之深淺。」夫曰：「悉聽。」醫乃以藥置龜頭，與婦行事。夫在旁觀之，乃曰：「若無這點藥在上面，我就疑心到底。」
stories.translation: The wife of a foolish man had an itchy sore in her private area and asked for medical treatment. 藟 The doctor, knowing the husband was foolish, said, "I must personally apply the medicine in order to determine how deep and severe the sore is." The husband replied, "As you wish." The doctor then placed the medicine on his own penis and had intercourse with the woman. The husband watched from the side and said, "If there were no medicine on it, I would have suspected something all along."

stories.text: 有觴客者，其妻每出酒一壺，即將鍋煤畫於臉上記數。主人索酒不已，童子曰：「少吃幾壺罷，家主婆臉上，看看有些不好看了。」
stories.translation: There was a wine guest whose wife, every time she poured out one pot of wine, would draw soot on her face to keep track. The host kept asking for more wine, and the servant boy said, "Please drink a few fewer pots. The mistress's face is starting to look quite unattractive."

stories.text: 蘇人遇一友云：「昨日兄為何如此高興，在家狠幹。」友云：「並不曾。」其人曰：「我在府上親聽甚久，還要賴麼？」友曰：「騙兄非人，我昨日實實不在家裡。」
stories.translation: A native of Suzhou met a friend and said, "Yesterday, why were you so happy at home, drinking heartily?" The friend replied, "I did not." The man said, "I heard it for a long time at your house. Are you going to deny it?" The friend replied, "To deceive you is not human-like. I was really not at home yesterday."

stories.text: 姦夫聞親夫歸，急欲潛遁，婦令其靜臥在床。夫至，問：「床上何人？」妻答云：「快莫做聲，隔壁王大爺被老娘打出來，權避在此。」夫大笑云：「這死烏龜，老婆值得恁怕！」
stories.translation: The adulterer, hearing that the husband was returning home, hurriedly wanted to sneak away, but the wife told him to lie still in bed. When the husband arrived, he asked, "Who is lying on the bed?" The wife replied, "Don't make a sound. Uncle Wang from next door was beaten out by my wife and is temporarily hiding here." The husband laughed heartily and said, "This dead turtle! Is your wife really worth such fear?"

stories.text: 夫妻相罵，夫恨曰：「臭娼根，我明日做了皇帝，就殺了你。」婦日夜懮泣不止，鄰女解之曰：「那有此事，不要聽他。」婦曰：「我家這個臭烏龜倒從不說謊的，自養的兒女，前年說要賣，當真的舊年都賣去了。」
stories.translation: A husband and wife were quarreling, and the husband angrily said, "You stinking prostitute! If I become emperor tomorrow, I will kill you." The wife wept and worried day and night. A neighbor's daughter comforted her, saying, "How could such a thing happen? Don't listen to him." The wife said, "My husband is a dishonest man who never lies. Last year he said he wanted to sell our children we raised ourselves, and indeed, the previous year he really sold them all."

stories.text: 有盜牛被枷者，親友問曰：「汝犯何罪至此。」盜牛者曰：「偶在街上走過，見地下有條草繩，以為沒用，誤拾而歸，故連此禍。」遇者曰：「誤拾草繩，有何罪犯？」盜牛者曰：「因繩上還有一物。」人問：「何物？」對曰：「是一隻小小耕牛。」
stories.translation: A man who had been put in stocks for stealing a cow was asked by relatives and friends, "What crime did you commit to end up like this?" The cow thief said, "I was just passing by the street when I saw a piece of grass rope on the ground. Thinking it useless, I mistakenly picked it up and took it home, so this disaster happened." The person present said, "Picking up a piece of grass rope by mistake, what crime is that?" The cow thief replied, "Because there was something else on the rope." Someone asked, "What thing?" He replied, "It was a small ox."

stories.text: 有持銀入市糴米，失叉袋於途，歸謂妻曰：「今日市中鬧甚，沒得好叉袋也。」妻曰：「你的莫非也沒了？」答曰：「隨你好漢便怎麼？」妻驚問：「銀子何在？」答曰：「這倒沒事，我緊緊拴好在叉袋角上。」
stories.translation: A man took silver to the market to buy rice but lost his satchel along the way. He returned home and told his wife, "The market was very crowded today; I couldn't find a good satchel." His wife asked, "Wasn't yours also lost?" He replied, "What if it's gone with your good-for-nothing?" The wife was startled and asked, "Where is the silver?" He replied, "That's not a problem. I tied it tightly to the corner of the satchel."

stories.text: 有行路者，對人門縫撒尿，為其家婦人看見，罵之不已。撒尿者曰：「我還是個童男，不消罵得。」婦曰：「頭多褪了一大截，還說甚麼童男！」鄰人笑曰：「這一句話，卻不該是娘子說的。」婦曰：「他明明欺我不在行，如何不指破他？」
stories.translation: A traveler urinated through a gap in someone's door, and was scolded repeatedly by a woman from the household who saw him. The man who urinated replied, "I'm still a virgin boy; there's no need to scold me." The woman said, "Your head has already lost a big chunk of hair. What are you talking about being a virgin?" A neighbor laughed and said, "This remark should not have come from the lady." The woman replied, "He clearly mocked me for being a novice. How could I not point it out?"

stories.text: 一人家費純用紋銀，或勸以傾銷八九色雜用，當有便宜。其人取元寶一錠，託熔八成。或素知其呆也，止傾四十兩付之，而利其餘。其人問：「元寶五十兩，為何反傾四十？」答曰：「五八得四十。」其人遽曰：「吾為公誤矣，用此等銀反無便益。」
stories.translation: A man spent pure ingot silver at home. Some advised him to melt down and mix in eight or nine types of mixed silver, which would be more cost-effective. The man took one ingot of silver and asked someone to melt it down into 80 percent. Someone who knew the man was foolish gave him only forty taels, keeping the rest for profit. The man asked, "If the silver ingot is fifty taels, why did you give me only forty?" The reply was, "Five eights make forty." The man immediately said, "I made a mistake for you. Using this kind of silver brings no benefit at all."

stories.text: 有應受官責者，以銀三錢，僱鄰人代往。其人得銀，欣然願替。既見官，官喝打三十。方受數杖，痛極，因私出所得銀，盡賄行杖者，得稍從輕。其人出謝前人曰：「蒙公賜銀救我性命，不然，幾乎打殺。」
stories.translation: A man who was supposed to receive official punishment paid three qian of silver to hire a neighbor to go in his place. The neighbor received the money and happily agreed to take his place. After meeting the official, the official ordered thirty lashes. While receiving only a few strokes, he was in extreme pain and secretly took out the silver he had received, giving it all to the official who administered the punishment, thus managing to have the beating slightly reduced. The man came out and thanked the previous person, saying, "I am grateful for your generous gift of silver that saved my life. Otherwise, I would have been nearly beaten to death."

stories.text: 有懷孕七個月即產一兒者，其夫恐養不大，遇人即問。一日，與友談及此事，友曰：「這個月無妨，我家祖亦是七個月出世的。」其人錯愕問曰：「若是這等說，令祖後來畢竟養得大否？」
stories.translation: A woman gave birth to a child after only seven months of pregnancy. Her husband, fearing the child would not survive, asked people he met for advice. One day, when discussing this with a friend, the husband said, "This month is fine. My ancestor was also born after seven months of pregnancy." The man asked in surprise, "If that's the case, did your ancestor eventually grow up to be a big person?"

stories.text: 兄謂弟曰：「卵袋若生翅膀，見有好婦人便可飛去。」弟曰：「使勿得，別人家個卵也要飛來個。」
stories.translation: The elder brother said to his younger brother, "If the scrotum could grow wings, whenever we saw a beautiful woman, we could fly away." The younger brother replied, "Don't be silly. If that were the case, someone else's scrotum would also fly over here."

stories.text: 新婦與新郎無緣，臨睡即踢打，不容近身。郎訴之父，父曰：「畢竟你有不是處，所以如此。」子云：「若不信，今晚你去睡一夜試試看。」
stories.translation: The new bride and groom had no affection for each other. When going to sleep, she would kick and hit him, not allowing him to come near her body. The groom complained to his father, who said, "After all, you must have done something wrong, so she treats you this way." The son said, "If you don't believe me, try sleeping with her for one night tonight and see what happens."

stories.text: 一人廿歲生子，其子專靠父膳，不能自立。一日算命云：「父壽八十，兒壽六十二。」其子大哭曰：「這兩年叫我如何過得去！」
stories.translation: A man had a son at twenty, and his son relied entirely on his father for food, unable to be independent. One day, after getting his fortune told, it was said, "The father will live to eighty, and the son to sixty-two." His son burst into tears and said, "How can I possibly survive these two years?"

stories.text: 鄉間坐凳，多以現成樹丫叉為腳者。一腳偶壞，主人命僕往山中覓取。僕持斧出，竟日空回，主人責之，答曰：「丫叉盡有，都是朝上生，沒有向下生的。」
stories.translation: In the countryside, many stools are made with existing tree forks as legs. When one leg happened to break, the owner ordered his servant to go into the mountains to find a replacement. The servant took an axe and went out, but returned empty-handed after a whole day. The owner scolded him, and the servant replied, "There are plenty of tree forks, but they all grow upward; there aren't any that grow downward."

stories.text: 一人命僕往楓橋打聽麥價，僕至橋，聞有呼「吃扯麵」者，以為不要錢的，連吃三碗逕走。賣麵者索錢不得，批其頦九下。急歸謂主人曰：「麥價打聽不出，麵價吾已曉矣。」主問：「如何？」答曰：「扯麵每碗要三個耳光。」
stories.translation: A man sent his servant to Fengqiao Bridge to inquire about wheat prices. When the servant arrived at the bridge, he heard someone shouting "Eat che mian!" and thought it was free, so he ate three bowls and left directly. The noodle seller, unable to collect payment, slapped the servant's chin nine times. In a hurry, he returned and told his master, "I couldn't find out the wheat price, but I already know the noodle price." The master asked, "How so?" He replied, "Each bowl of che mian requires three slaps."

stories.text: 一人睡在床上，仰面背痛，覆臥肚痛，側困腰痛，坐起臀痛，百醫無效。或勸其翻床，及翻動，見褥底鐵秤錘一個，墊在下面。
stories.translation: A man was lying in bed, with back pain when lying on his back, stomach pain when lying face down, waist pain when lying on his side, and buttock pain when sitting up. No doctors could cure him. Someone advised him to turn the bed over, and upon flipping it, they found an iron weight for a scale underneath the mattress.

stories.text: 有人極懶者，臥而懶起，家人喚之吃飯，復懶應。良久，度其必飢，乃哀懇之。徐曰：「懶吃得。」家人曰：「不吃便死，如何使得？」復搖首漫應曰：「我亦懶活矣。」
stories.translation: There was a man who was extremely lazy. He lay in bed and was too lazy to get up, and even when his family called him for meals, he was too lazy to respond. After a long time, thinking that he must be hungry, they earnestly pleaded with him. He slowly said, "I'm too lazy to eat." The family members said, "If you don't eat, you will die. How can that be allowed?" He shook his head again and replied indifferently, "I'm also too lazy to live."

stories.text: 一人素性最懶，終日偃臥不起。每日三餐，亦懶於動口，懨懨絕粒，竟至餓斃。冥王以其生前性懶，罰去輪迴變貓。懶者曰：「身上毛片，願求大王賞一全體黑身，單單留一白鼻，感恩實多。」王問何故，答曰：「我做貓躲在黑地裏，鼠見我白鼻，認作是塊米糕，貪想愉吃，潛到嘴邊，一口咬住，豈不省了無數氣力。」
stories.translation: A man had always been extremely lazy, lying in bed all day without getting up. For the three meals each day, he was also too lazy to speak, and gradually stopped eating solid food altogether, eventually starving to death. The King of Hell punished him for his laziness in life by sentencing him not to be reborn but instead transformed into a cat. The lazy man said, "I have patches of fur on my body. I humbly request the Great King to grant me a completely black body, leaving only a white nose; your kindness would be deeply appreciated." The King asked why, and he replied, "When I become a cat hiding in the dark, mice will see my white nose and mistake it for a piece of rice cake. They'll greedily try to steal and eat it, sneaking up to my mouth, where I can bite them right away—wouldn't that save me countless efforts?"

stories.text: 一人偶見露水桌子，因以指戲寫「謀篡」字樣，被一仇家見之，奪桌就走，往府首告。及官坐堂，露水以為日色曝乾，字迹減去。官問何事，其人無可說得，慌稟曰：「小人有桌子一堂，特把這張來看樣，不知老爺要買否？」
stories.translation: A man once saw a dew-covered table and, out of idle curiosity, used his finger to write the words "mou cun" (plotting to usurp) on it. A rival who happened to see this seized the table and ran off to report it at the government office. By the time the official sat in court, he thought the sunlight had dried up the dew, and the writing had faded away. The official asked what the matter was, and since there was nothing to say, the man nervously reported, "I have a set of tables at home. I specially brought this one for you to see as an example. I wonder if Your Honor would like to buy it?"

stories.text: 一鄉人穿新漿布衣入城，因出門甚早，衣為露水諷濕。及至城中，怪其頓軟。事畢出城，衣為日色曝乾，又硬如故。歸謂妻曰：「莫說鄉下人進城再硬不起來，連鄉下人的衣服見了城裡人的衣服，都會綿軟起來。」
stories.translation: A villager wearing a new starched cloth robe went into the city. Because he had left home very early, his clothes were dampened by dew. By the time he arrived in the city, he found it suddenly soft. After finishing his business and leaving the city, the sun dried his clothes again, making them hard as before. He returned home and told his wife, "Don't say that a man from the countryside can't become hard (i.e., assertive) after entering the city; even the clothes of people from the countryside soften when they see the clothes of city dwellers."

stories.text: 鄉民入城赴席，見椅桌多懸桌圍坐褥。歸謂人曰：「莫說城裏人受用，連城裡的椅桌都是極受用的。」人問其故，答曰：「桌子穿了繡花裙，椅子都是穿銷金背心的。」
stories.translation: A villager went to the city for a banquet and saw that many chairs and tables were equipped with hanging table skirts and padded cushions. He returned home and said to others, "Don't just say that city dwellers enjoy comforts; even the chairs and tables in the city are extremely comfortable." People asked him why, and he replied, "The tables wear embroidered skirts, and the chairs are all wearing gold-embroidered vests."

stories.text: 甲乙兩鄉人入城，偶吃醃蛋，甲駭曰：「同一蛋也，此味獨何以鹹？」乙曰：「我知之矣，決定是醃鴨哺的。」
stories.translation: Two villagers, Jia and Yi, went into the city and happened to eat salted eggs. Jia was startled and said, "It's the same kind of egg; why is this one uniquely salty?" Yi replied, "I know now. It must be a salted duck's egg."

stories.text: 有演《琵琶記》而找《關公斬貂蟬》者，鄉人見之泣曰：「好個孝順媳婦，辛苦了一生，竟被那紅臉蠻子害了。」
stories.translation: There was a performance of The Pipa Record that mistakenly played Guan Gong Slays Diao Chan. A villager watching it wept and said, "What an obedient daughter-in-law! She toiled her whole life, only to be killed by that red-faced savage."

stories.text: 有演《琵琶記》者，找戲是《荊釵．逼嫁》，忽有人嘆曰：「戲不可不看，極是長學問的。今日方知蔡伯喈的母親，就是王十朋的丈母。」
stories.translation: There was a performance of The Pipa Record, and the next play mistakenly performed was Jing Chai: Forced Marriage. Suddenly, someone sighed and said, "Plays are something you must watch; they're extremely educational. Today I've learned that Cai Bojie's mother is actually Wang Shipeng's mother-in-law."

stories.text: 一痴人聞盜入門，急寫「各有內外」四字，貼於堂上。聞盜已登堂，又寫「此路不通」四字，貼于內室。聞盜復至，乃逃入廁中。盜蹤跡及之，乃掩廁門咳嗽曰：「有人在此。」
stories.translation: A foolish man heard that a thief had entered his house and hastily wrote the four characters "gou you neiwai" (literally, "each has inside and outside"), pasting them on the hall. Hearing that the thief had already entered the hall, he wrote another four characters, "ci lu bu tong" (literally, "this road is not passable"), and pasted them on the inner room. Hearing that the thief was coming again, he fled into the toilet. The thief followed his trail and reached him, then covered the toilet door and coughed, saying, "Someone is here."

stories.text: 一人偶撲地，方爬起復跌。乃曰：「啐！早知還有只一跌，便不走起來也罷了。」
stories.translation: A man accidentally fell to the ground, had just climbed up again when he fell down once more. He said, "Spit!" "If I had known there was going to be another fall, I would have just stayed on the ground."

stories.text: 一人善踱，行步甚遲。日將晡矣，巡夜者于城外見之，問以何往，曰：「欲至府前。」巡夜者即指犯夜，擒捉送官。其人辯曰：「天色甚早，何為犯夜？」曰：「你如此踱法，踱至府前，極早也是二更了。」
stories.translation: A man was good at strolling, and walked very slowly. As dusk approached, a night patrol officer saw him outside the city walls and asked where he was going. He replied, "I want to go to the front of the government office." The night patrol officer immediately accused him of violating curfew and arrested him for delivery to the authorities. The man protested, "It's still very early; how can this be a violation of curfew?" They replied, "With the way you stroll, by the time you reach in front of the government office, even if it's early, it will already be the second watch."

stories.text: 有酷好乘馬者，被人所欺，以五十金買駑馬一匹。不堪鞭策，乃僱舟載馬，而身跨其上。既行里許，嫌其遲慢，謂舟人曰：「我買酒請你，與我快些搖，我要出轡頭哩。」
stories.translation: There was a man who greatly loved riding horses. After being cheated by someone, he bought an old and weak horse for fifty taels of gold. Unable to endure whipping the horse, he hired a boat to carry the horse while he rode on it himself. After traveling about a li, he found the pace too slow and said to the boatman, "I'll buy you some wine. Row faster for me; I want to get out of this bridle head."

stories.text: 鋪司遞緊急公文，官恐其遲，撥一馬騎之。其人趕馬而行，人問其「如此急事，何不乘馬？」答曰：「六隻腳走，豈不快如四隻。」
stories.translation: The post office was delivering urgent official documents. The officer, fearing delays, assigned a horse for the rider to ride. The man urged his horse forward. Someone asked him, "Such an urgent matter—why not ride the horse?" He replied, "With six legs running, wouldn't it be faster than with four?"

stories.text: 一婦人與人私通，正在房中行事，丈夫叩門。婦即將此人裝入米袋內，立于門背後。丈夫入見，問曰：「叉袋裏是甚麼？」婦人著忙，不能對答。其人從叉袋中應聲曰：「米。」
stories.translation: A woman was having an affair with another man and was just in the middle of their tryst when her husband knocked on the door. The woman quickly stuffed the man into a rice sack and stood it behind the door. Her husband entered and asked, "What's in that bag?" The woman was flustered and could not answer. The man inside the sack replied, "Rice."

stories.text: 有賣鵝者，因要出恭，置鵝在地。登廁後，一人以鴨換去。其人解畢，出視嘆曰：「奇哉！才一時不見，如何便餓得恁般黑瘦了。」
stories.translation: A man selling geese, needing to relieve himself, placed the goose on the ground. After using the toilet, another person replaced the goose with a duck. When he finished and came out to look, he sighed, "Strange!" Just a short time away, how could it have become so thin and dark from hunger?"

stories.title_en: Using a Hat as a Fan
stories.text: 有暑月帶氈帽而出者，歇大樹下乘涼，即脫帽以當扇。扇訖，謂人曰：「今日若不帶此帽出來，幾乎熱殺。」
stories.translation: A man went out in the hot summer wearing a felt hat. After resting under a big tree for shade, he immediately took off his hat to use as a fan. After fanning himself, he told someone, "If I hadn't brought this hat today, I would have almost been roasted to death."

stories.text: 一人見賣海螄者，喚住要買，問：「幾多錢一斤？」賣者笑曰：「從來海螄是量的。」其人喝曰：「這難道不曉得！問你幾多錢一尺？」
stories.translation: A man saw a vendor selling sea snails, called him over to buy some, and asked, "How much per catty?" The seller laughed and said, "Sea snails are always measured by volume." The man shouted, "How could you not know this!" He asked, "Then how much per chi?"

stories.text: 一人極好靜，而所居介於銅，鐵兩匠之間，朝夕聒耳，甚苦之，常曰：「此兩家若有遷居之日，我寧可作東款謝。」一日，二匠並至曰：「我等欲遷矣，足下素許東道，特來叩領。」其人大喜，遂盛款之。席間問之曰：「汝兩家遷往何處？」答曰：「他搬在我屋裡，我即搬在他屋裡。」
stories.translation: A man greatly loved quietness, but his home was situated between a copperworker and an ironworker. The constant noise from morning to night was deafening and very troubling for him. He often said, "If these two families ever decided to move house, I would be willing to host them as the guest of honor." One day, both craftsmen came together and said, "We want to move now. You have long promised to be our host; we've come especially to ask for your hospitality." The man was overjoyed and entertained them lavishly. During the banquet, he asked them, "Where are your two families moving to?" They replied, "He is moving into my house, and I am moving into his house."

stories.text: 有人在混堂洗浴，掬水入口而嗽之。眾各攢眉相向，惡其不潔。此人貯水於手曰：「諸公不要愁，待我嗽完之後，吐出外面去。」
stories.translation: A man was bathing in a mixed bathhouse and scooped up water to rinse his mouth. The others all frowned at him, disgusted by the uncleanliness. Holding water in his hand, this man said, "Gentlemen, don't worry; after I finish rinsing my mouth, I will spit it out outside."

stories.text: 一人賦性呆蠢，不通文墨。途遇一友，友問曰：「兄何往？」此人茫然不答，乃記「何往」二字以問人。人知其呆，故為戲之曰：「此惡語罵兄耳。」其人含怒而別。次日，復遇前友問：「兄何往？」此人遽憤然曰：「我是不何往，你倒要何往哩！」
stories.translation: A man was naturally dull and stupid, illiterate. On the road he met a friend, who asked him, "Brother, where are you going?" The man was at a loss and did not answer, so he wrote down the two characters "he wang" to ask someone else. People knew of his stupidity and thus teased him by saying, "This is just a vulgar insult directed at you." The man left in anger. The next day, he met the same friend again and asked, "Brother, where are you heading?" This man suddenly became angry and said, "I am not going anywhere, but why do you want to go somewhere!"

stories.text: 一人問大辟，臨刑，對劊子手曰：「銅刀借一把來動手，我一生服何首烏的。」
stories.translation: A man was about to be executed by capital punishment and, facing the executioner, said, "Lend me a copper knife for a moment; I have been taking Polygonum multiflorum all my life."

stories.text: 有平素酷信陰陽，一日被牆壓倒。家人欲亟救，其人伸出頭來曰：「且慢，待我忍著，你去問問陰陽，今日可動得土否？」
stories.translation: There was a man who intensely believed in yin and yang. One day, he was knocked down by a wall. His family wanted to rescue him immediately, but the man stuck his head out and said, "Wait a moment. I'll endure it for now; you go ask about yin and yang whether the earth can be moved today."

stories.text: 一婦人在門首，被人注目而看，婦人大罵不已。鄰嫗勸曰：「你又不在內室，憑他看看何妨？」婦曰：「我若把好面孔看看也罷，被這樣呆臉看了，豈不苦毒。」
stories.translation: A woman was at the door when someone stared at her. The woman kept cursing without stopping. A neighborly old woman advised, "You are not in your private room; let them look if they want to." The woman said, "If people looked at my pretty face, it would be fine. But to be stared at by such a dull and ugly face—wouldn't that be painful?"

stories.text: 一老翁冬夜醉臥，置腳爐于被中，誤爇其腿。早起罵鄉鄰曰：「悉老人家多吃了幾杯酒，睡著了，便自不知。你們這班後生，竟不來喚醒一聲，難道燒人臭也不曉得！」
stories.translation: An old man, drunk on a winter night, lay down and placed a foot warmer inside his blanket, accidentally burning his leg. The next morning he scolded the neighbors, saying, "It's all because old men drank a few more cups of wine and fell asleep without realizing it." "You young people didn't even come to wake me up. Don't you know the smell of burning flesh!"

stories.text: 有兄弟共買一靴，兄日著以拜客赴宴。弟不甘服，亦每夜穿之，環行室中，直至達旦。俄而靴敝，兄再議合買，弟曰：「我要睡矣。」
stories.translation: There were brothers who jointly bought a pair of boots, and the elder brother wore them every day to visit guests and attend banquets. The younger brother was unwilling to accept this and also wore them each night, walking around the room in circles until dawn. Soon the boots were worn out, and the elder brother suggested buying a new pair together again. The younger brother said, "I want to sleep now."

stories.text: 兩人對奕象棋，傍觀者教不至口。其一大怒，揮拳擊之，痛極卻步。右手麼臉，左手遙指曰：「還不叉士！」
stories.translation: Two people were playing xiangqi (Chinese chess) against each other, and a bystander could not stop talking to give advice. One of them became very angry, swung his fist at the bystander, but took a painful step back instead. With his right hand he touched his face and with his left hand pointed afar, saying, "Haven't you moved the shi yet!"

stories.text: 一呆子見有以髮換糖者，謬謂凡物皆可換也。晨起，袖中藏髮一料以往，遇酒肆即入飽餐。餐畢，以髮與之。肆佣皆笑，其人怒曰：「他人俱當錢用，到我偏用不得耶！」爭辯良久，肆佣因揪髮亂打。其人徐理髮曰：「整料的與他偏不要，反在我頭上來亂搶。」
stories.translation: A foolish man saw someone exchanging hair for candy and mistakenly thought that anything could be exchanged. The next morning, he went out with a bundle of hair hidden in his sleeve, and whenever he passed an inn, he would go in for a hearty meal. After the meal, he gave them the hair. The inn staff all laughed, and the man became angry, saying, "Everyone else can use it as money; why can't I?" After a long argument, the inn staff grabbed his hair and beat him up. The man slowly combed his hair and said, "They didn't want the neatly bundled one I gave them, yet they came to grab it messily from my head."
